subject: Animation
title: Animation Education Goes Global
description: A quick, practical guide to Animation Education Goes Global.

hook.text: Elite animation schools exist on every continent now, from France's Gobelins to Korea's KAIST to CalArts in the U.S.

buildup.text: These schools produce graduates who work for studios worldwide, creating a truly global talent pipeline.

discovery.text: Online courses and free tools like Blender now let anyone learn animation regardless of geography or wealth.

twist.text: The democratization of education means talent can emerge from anywhere — but jobs still cluster in a few cities.

climax.text: Animation education is globalizing faster than animation employment, creating both opportunity and frustration.

punchline.text: Anyone can learn to animate now. Finding a job is another story.

quiz.question: What challenge does global animation education create?
options: There are too few animation schools worldwide
Education has globalized faster than employment, so talent can emerge anywhere but jobs still cluster in few cities
Online courses have replaced all in-person programs

details.summary: Animation education has expanded globally, with excellent programs now operating far beyond traditional centers. Schools in France, South Korea, India, Brazil, and across Africa are training the next generation of global animation talent.
details.whyItMatters: Distributed animation education democratizes who can become an animator and what stories get told. As training globalizes, animation perspectives widen and the industry becomes genuinely international.
takeaways: Animation schools now operate in dozens of countries beyond traditional hubs
France's Gobelins remains the world's most prestigious animation school
Global education creates a more diverse and capable animation workforce

faq.question: What are the world's leading animation schools?
faq.answer: France's Gobelins is widely considered the best. CalArts in the US, Sheridan in Canada, and the Royal College of Art in the UK are also top-tier. Increasingly, strong programs in South Korea, India, and Brazil are producing globally competitive graduates.

faq.question: How has online learning changed animation education?
faq.answer: Online platforms like Animation Mentor and School of Motion make professional training accessible worldwide. Students in countries without physical animation schools can now access instruction from industry professionals, dramatically lowering barriers to entry.
